question: What will President Lee Jae-myung's job approval rating be in Gallup Korea's weekly poll released on November 27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Gallup approval flat 39-41 for five weeks; latest 39% (Nov 10-12). Reference class: two-week-ahead readings of a stable Gallup Korea presidential approval series, typically within ±3 pts. Concurrent trackers show no sharp move: Realmeter 36.4% (+0.5, Nov 9-13; structurally ~2-3 pts below Gallup), NBS 44% (-2, Nov 9-11). Downside risks: housing-policy discontent, partisan fights over special counsel / Chief Justice impeachment, NBS showing 30s collapse; upside: export/investment news, previous floor at 37% (Sept record low). No human market prices this quantity (Polymarket only has 'Lee out in 2026' at 3%, irrelevant). Median 39, modest symmetric spread.
calls.dossier:
- Gallup Korea 제682호 (fieldwork Nov 10-12, 2026, n=1,002): approval 39% (-2), disapproval 50%, undecided 10%; DP 39%, PPP 26%. Positive reasons: economy/livelihood 19%, diplomacy 17%; negative: real estate 17%, economy 15%, morality/own trial 12% (rising). [Hankook Ilbo / iMBC, Nov 13]
- Gallup recent weekly series: 39 (Oct 13-15), 40 (Oct 20-22), 39 (Oct 27-29), 41 (Nov 3-5), 39 (Nov 10-12). [question background]
- Gallup longer series: 44% mid-Aug 2026 (then a record low, negatives 46%); 40% early Sep; 38% Sep 11; 37% Sep 18 (all-time low, disapproval 56%); recovered to ~39-41 by October. [fnnews Aug 14; mt.co.kr Sep 4; nate Sep 11/18]
- Realmeter (Nov 9-13, n=2,512): 36.4% (+0.5). Realmeter usually reads below Gallup. Party support DP 34.6 vs PPP 43.0 (different methodology). Cited positives: Chungcheong investment, chip exports; negatives: party-presidential office disagreement on property tax reform, special-counsel standoff, stock-market jitters. [fnnews / Hankook Ilbo, Nov 16]
- NBS (Nov 9-11, n=1,001): 44% (-2 vs two weeks earlier), negative 47% (+3); Seoul 34%; people in their 30s at 28% (down from 44%); 51% say cut back the president's direct SNS communication. [businesspost / Hankook Ilbo, Nov 12]
- Upcoming events: Supreme Court full bench hears Han Duck-soo insurrection appeal Nov 19 (detention expires Nov 20); push to impeach / investigate Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae; budget subcommittee markup Nov 16-27; housing-supply bills blocked by PPP; Han's separate first-instance sentencing Nov 30 (after the window).
- Status quo outcome: a reading near the recent 39-41 band.
- Spread of 2-week changes in Gallup over Aug-Nov 2026: mostly within ±2-3 pts, with the largest moves (~-3 to -4) during the Aug-Sep slide.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the Gallup Korea Daily Opinion weekly report dated Fri Nov 27, 2026 (or Nov 26), nationwide '잘하고 있다' integer %, not Realmeter/NBS.
- Event window: fieldwork ~Nov 24-26 -> report Nov 27, 2026; as of Nov 16, 0% of fieldwork elapsed (one intermediate Gallup release, Nov 20, comes first).
- Market: no human market on this quantity; Polymarket only has 'Lee out as president in 2026'.
- Searched but not found: Gallup report dated Nov 20 (not yet published); any shock events planned for Nov 17-26.

calls.reasoning: Gallup approval has been between 37% and 41% since mid-September; the last 5 readings were 39, 40, 39, 41, 39. The target report (fieldwork ~Nov 24-26) is two weeks past the last reading, so the status-quo median is ~39. Other trackers disagree in both directions: NBS at 44% (down 2), Realmeter at 36.4% (up 0.5) with the Democratic Party at its post-inauguration low. Downside risks: housing bills stalling (the top disapproval reason), budget fights, the Han Duck-soo and Chief Justice impeachment controversy. Upside: diplomatic events, a rebound toward the 40-41 tops. No matching human market: the Polymarket contract on Lee leaving office in 2026 (3%) has nothing to do with the approval level. Tail escapes outside 31.5-46.5 are about 1% each, so none were declared.

calls.reasoning: Gallup approval has been boxed at 37-41 since mid-September; the last five readings are 39, 40, 39, 41, 39 and the latest (Nov 10-12) is 39. The target report's fieldwork (~Nov 24-26) is two weeks past that reading. Realmeter is stable (36.4%, +0.5); NBS dipped to 44% (-2), with the 30s subgroup falling and 'morality/trial' rising as a disapproval reason, which gives a mild downside lean. Upcoming catalysts (Han Duck-soo Supreme Court hearing, Chief Justice impeachment push, budget markup, stalled housing bills) are not regime-breaking. Median 39, SD ~2. calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the Gallup series (39,40,39,41,39; Sep low 37; Oct readings of 37 per Run 2), Realmeter 36.4 and NBS 44. One minor factual inconsistency (Run 1 calling the mid-Aug 44% a 'record low') is best read as the low at the time it was reported; it doesn't affect the forecast and couldn't be checked without web access. The remaining disputes are judgment: how much the mixed tracker signals (NBS -2 with the 30s subgroup down, Realmeter flat) tilt the distribution (a slight lower tail, median unchanged at 39), and whether to price escapes outside 31.5-46.5 (no concrete mechanism within two weeks, so none declared). I agree with the runs' reference class and ~2pt two-week SD and carry it forward, with width set from that SD rather than from the runs' numbers.
